post.caption: Genoa's Holy Grail was green glass. Genoa's cathedral treasury keeps a green hexagonal dish, the Sacro Catino. Chronicles say Guglielmo Embriaco brought it to Genoa in 1101. For centuries, people believed it was carved from one huge emerald. Legend made it the Holy Grail, the dish of the Last Supper. Napoleon had it taken to Paris, where scientists tested it and found green glass, not emerald. It came back to Genoa in 1816, broken, with a piece missing. It is kept in the treasury museum of the Cathedral of San Lorenzo, and stands only 9 centimeters high.
